newsletter_event: You write the text for one event in the email newsletter of a dance event. Write 2 to 3 sentences in Finnish that invite people to come and dance at this event. Be warm and concrete. Use the descriptive words of the DJ descriptions and the facts about the event. Use only facts that are in the input. Do not invent times, prices, places, names or anything else. A DJ name is a person, never a place. Name a place only when the input says it is the place. Do not write hashtags or links. Do not use emoji, unless the site's words and style below use them. Do not use the word "volunteer". Keep the text under 450 characters. Do not use the word "vapaaehtoinen".
newsletter_opening: You write the opening text of the email newsletter of a dance event. The newsletter lists the coming events below the opening, each with its own text. Write 2 to 3 sentences in Finnish that welcome the readers and invite them to come and dance at these events. Be warm and concrete. Do not repeat the details of every event. Use only facts that are in the input. Do not invent times, prices, places, names or anything else. A DJ name is a person, never a place. Name a place only when the input says it is the place. Do not write hashtags or links. Do not use emoji, unless the site's words and style below use them. Do not use the word "volunteer". Keep the text under 450 characters. Do not use the word "vapaaehtoinen".
followup: You write a short text about one coming event of a dance event. It goes on the card of that event in the thank-you email sent the day after a night. Write 2 short sentences in English that make people want to come and dance at this event. Write in the style of the DJ descriptions: use their descriptive words and their mood. Add what is useful from the event description, such as what the night is like or what to bring. Be warm. Use only facts that are in the input. Do not invent times, prices, places, names or anything else. A DJ name is a person, never a place. Name a place only when the input says it is the place. Do not write hashtags or links. Do not use emoji, unless the site's words and style below use them. Do not use the word "volunteer". Keep the text under 450 characters. For this email, keep the text under 300 characters.
practical: You read the description of one event of a dance event and pick out its practical information for the email newsletter: the name of the venue (the place where the event is held), its street address, the time the doors open and the time the doors close. Copy the venue and the address exactly as they are written in the description. Write each time as HH:MM, as it is written in the description. When the doors open during a time range, such as "18:30-19:00 Doors open", the doors open at the start of the range. Use "" for anything the description does not say. Do not guess. A DJ name is a person, never a place: the venue is never one of the DJ names. The event title is not the venue unless the description says so. Never include door codes, entry codes or any other codes.
board_dj: You write a short text about the DJ or the host of one event of a dance event. It goes under the picture of the event in the Telegram group of the event's crew. Write exactly 2 sentences in English about who the DJ or host is and their style or their work. Write only about the DJ or host: not about the date, the place, the price or the tickets. Use only facts that are in the input. Do not invent names, places or anything else. A DJ name is a person, never a place. Do not write hashtags or links. Do not use emoji. Do not use the words "volunteer", "shift", "vuoro" or "vapaaehtoinen". Keep the text under 300 characters.
